title: Enterprise Onboarding 1 Comprehensive Playbook (Onboarding, Integration, Escalation, QBRs)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines Redwood’s standard process for enterprise customer onboarding, technical integration, health checks and QBRs, and the escalation path for production incidents. It’s intended for Customer Success (CSMs), Solutions Engineering (SE), Oncall SRE, and Sales/Account teams.

Scope: Applies to all enterprise accounts (contracted Dedicated or Private customers and high-volume Hosted customers) from kickoff through steady-state handoff.

Owners and Roles

- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Asha Patel)
- CSM: single point of contact for customer relationship, commercial milestones, and QBR coordination
- Solutions Engineer: technical lead for integration, API validation, and early performance tuning
- Oncall SRE / Platform Oncall: responsible for production incidents and escalations
- Product/PM: feature/roadmap decisions and prioritization as needed

Onboarding Phases (high level)

1) Pre-Kickoff (Contract signed)
   - Deliverables: Welcome packet, onboarding timeline, named team contacts, initial access request form.
   - Actions: CSM sends Welcome packet within 24 business hours. SE schedules technical kickoff within 3 business days.

2) Technical Kickoff (Day 0-7)
   - Agenda: success criteria, architecture review, network/firewall requirements, auth/KMS plan, data residency requirements.
   - Checklist (SE):
     - Confirm account type (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
     - Provide API keys / service accounts or private control plane access instructions
     - Verify network egress/ingress rules for dedicated pools or private control plane
     - Confirm KMS/HSM integration plan if required

3) Integration & Validation (Week 1-4)
   - Goals: successful end-to-end calls to redwood-api; baseline latency and correctness tests; run canonical prompt set.
   - Integration checklist:
     - Call generation endpoint with test prompt and check streaming behavior
     - Validate embeddings endpoint and vector dimensionality for chosen model
     - Confirm rate limits and quotas with CSM/Account team
     - For Dedicated/Private: deploy sample workload to staging and verify autoscaling policies
   - Recommended commands / examples (SE):
     - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'
     - Observe response streaming and tokenization behavior in logs

4) Performance Tuning and Quality Guardrails (Week 2-6)
   - Actions: enable prefix caching where applicable, tune batching parameters, evaluate quantization profile if on Dedicated hardware.
   - Deliverables: recommended config (batch_size, max_tokens, kv_cache_policy), sample prompts for regression monitoring.

5) Handoff to Success + QBR Cadence (After steady state)
   - Handoff checklist: documented runbook, contact list, SLO/SLA expectations, escalation contacts.
   - QBR cadence: quarterly by default; monthly for strategic accounts.

Escalation Playbook (Production)

Severity definitions and expected responses:
- Sev1 (Critical): total platform outage or customer-impacting functionality down (major revenue impact). Response ETA: 15 minutes. Oncall SRE paged. CSM informs customer within 30 minutes.
- Sev2 (High): degraded performance causing reduced service quality (e.g., P95 latency breach, partial failovers). Response ETA: 60 minutes.
- Sev3 (Medium): limited customer impact, workaround available. Response ETA: 4 business hours.
- Sev4 (Low): informational, feature request, or scheduled maintenance items. Response ETA: next business day.

Escalation steps (ordered):
1) Customer contacts support via one of the following channels: support@redwood.ai (email), in-app support widget, or dedicated enterprise Slack channel.
2) Tier 1 Support (CS + Support Engineers) triages - collect logs, request request IDs, timestamps, and example API calls.
3) If unresolved and meets Sev1/2 criteria, escalate to Oncall SRE via PagerDuty (team: rd-platform-oncall).
4) SEs and Product are looped in for root cause analysis and customer communication.
5) Post-incident: publish incident summary, customer-facing timeline, and remediation plan within 72 hours for Sev1/2.

Contact matrix (examples):
- Support email: support@redwood.ai
- Enterprise Slack: #cs-enterprise-<account-name>
- PagerDuty: rd-platform-oncall (primary), rd-fw-oncall (fallback)
- Escalation lead: (CS Director) Maria Chen

Support Process and SLAs

- Channels: email, portal, Slack, phone (for Sev1 after hours)
- Initial response targets: 15m (Sev1), 1h (Sev2), 4h (Sev3), 24h (Sev4)
- Resolution SLA: negotiated per-contract. Default guidance: 24h for Sev2, 72h for Sev3.
- Escalation ownership: Support Engineers handle Triage -> SE takes ownership of integration issues -> Oncall SRE owns production incident remediations.

Health Checks and QBR Template

Standard account health metrics to monitor before each QBR:
- Availability SLO: 99.9% (daily rolling window)
- Latency SLOs: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 400ms for generation APIs on standard models (hosted); Dedicated SLAs may differ per contract
- Error rate: < 0.5% 5xx errors on API calls
- Cost per 1k tokens: baseline and delta vs prior quarter
- Cache hit rate (if enabled): target > 60% for steady-state prefix-heavy workloads
- Throughput: requests/sec and tokens/sec observed during peak windows

QBR agenda (30-60 minutes):
1) Executive summary: adoption, MRR impact, top wins and blockers
2) Health snapshot: key metrics and trends (availability, latency, error rate, cost)
3) Feature/roadmap alignment: upcoming product changes that impact the customer
4) Operational review: incidents since last QBR and mitigations
5) Action items and owners: prioritized list with due dates

Template: include a one-page snapshot (use Console dashboard) and a short slide deck with 6-8 slides. Attach: runbooks, recent incident reports, and performance tuning recommendations.

Known Issues & Workarounds (selected list)

1) Issue: Occasional streaming stall on long prompt chains when network MTU is constrained
   - Workaround: Reduce chunk size by setting streaming_chunk_size to 512 and reattempt connection. SEs can apply temporary proxy buffer tuning.

2) Issue: Higher-than-expected P95 latency for small, high-QPS requests on Dedicated pools under burst
   - Workaround: Configure a small dedicated burst capacity (policy: reserved + burst 10%) and enable request-level priority for critical routes.

3) Issue: 401 / 403 auth errors after rotating keys in customer KMS integration
   - Workaround: Confirm new key material is propagated to private control plane and restart connector service (systemctl restart redwood-kms-connector).

4) Issue: Embedding dimensional mismatch when migrating between model variants
   - Workaround: Run migration validation script to reindex vectors and update downstream vector DB mapping. Example: python scripts/reindex_embeddings.py --model rwd-embed-v2

Operational Artifacts to Deliver to Customer

- Runbook: customer-specific runbook including: quick checks, log locations, runbook steps for common failures.
- Access list: team contacts, PagerDuty rotations, Service Accounts and expiry dates.
- Test scripts: canonical prompt set, load test harness, and synthetic traffic generator.

Handoff Checklist (CS -> Customer Success steady state)

- Completed integration validation and signed acceptance test results.
- Runbooks and playbooks documented in the customer Confluence space.
- QBR schedule agreed and initial QBR deck shared.
- Escalation contacts verified and PagerDuty integrated.

Reporting and Postmortem Policy

- For Sev1/Sev2 incidents affecting the customer, a postmortem is required within 7 business days. PMs and Engineering must provide RCA, timeline, impact assessment, and remediation plan.
- Customer-facing summary is aligned by CS and Product before distribution.

Appendices

A. Sample Acceptance Test (checklist)
- Successful generation call with streaming enabled
- Embedding creation and retrieval validated in sample vector DB
- Baseline latency within 25% of Redwood-hosted baseline for selected model
- Security checklist: KMS integration tested, TLS certs validated, network rules confirmed

B. Quick CLI snippets
- Basic generate call: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"prompt":"Test"}'
- Health endpoint (internal): curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' https://internal.health.redwood.ai/healthz

C. Links and References
- Internal runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- SLO & error budget guidance: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Dedicated deployment guide: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides

End of playbook
